title: Find Latest Group of Size M
summary: Given an array representing a permutation of numbers from 1 to n, and a binary string of size n initially set to all zeros, set the bit at position arr[i] to 1 for each step i from 1 to n.
statement: Given an array representing a permutation of numbers from 1 to n, and a binary string of size n initially set to all zeros, set the bit at position arr[i] to 1 for each step i from 1 to n. Find the latest step where a contiguous substring of exactly m ones exists, which cannot be extended in either direction. Return the step number if such a group exists, otherwise return -1.
constraints: arr is a permutation of positions one through n, activated in order.
Return the latest one-based step containing at least one maximal consecutive-one group of exactly length m, or -1.
reference_solution:
def latest_exact_one_group(arr, m):
 n=len(arr)
 if m==n:return n
 length=[0]*(n+2);groups=0;answer=-1
 for step,position in enumerate(arr,1):
  left,right=length[position-1],length[position+1]
  if left==m:groups-=1
  if right==m:groups-=1
  merged=left+1+right;length[position-left]=length[position+right]=merged
  if merged==m:groups+=1
  if groups:answer=step
 return answer

hints: Track the lengths at both endpoints of every active group.
When a position activates, remove neighboring groups of size m from the count, merge their lengths, and add the merged group if its size is m.
Record each step where the count remains positive.
Endpoint lengths are sufficient because only groups adjacent to the new position can change.
